newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium's Frere buys 2.9 pct of Suez from Elf.
newsitem.headline: Belgium's Frere buys 2.9 pct of Suez from Elf.

text.p: Belgian financier Albert Frere snapped up five million shares in French holding company Suez on Monday in the latest of a series of asset sales by French oil group Elf Acquitaine.
Belgian Electrafina, a unit of Frere's Groupe Bruxelles Lambert, said it would pay Elf about six billion Belgian francs ($190.5 million) for the 2.9 percent stake.
"We are taking the stake with Suez's blessing," Electrafina chief executive officer Thierry de Rudder said.

"The Suez acquisition was an opportunity which presented itself. It is a good financial investment. It also shows our good understanding with the chief executive officer of Suez (Gerard Mestrallet)," he added.
He declined to say whether the GBL-Electrafina group planned further acquisitions of Suez stock.
Elf said the sale was in line with its policy of divesting financial and non-strategic industrial assets to raise 10 billion French francs.
Since the start of 1996, Elf has sold its interests in Belgian oil group Petrofina (which is controlled by Electrafina) and French conglomerate Compagnie Generale des Eaux.
Last Thursday, it also sold its entire 7.06 percent stake, or 1,787,793 shares, in Belgium's Compagnie Nationale a Portefeuille (CNP), another company in Frere's business empire.
An Elf spokesman said other asset sales were still on the cards. ($ = 31.49 Belgian Francs)
